context_for_next_testing_agent: This iteration exclusively covered the deploy/linux/install_systemd_services.sh custom-directory sed-substitution fix (lines 189-200). Verified via direct simulation (copied momentumx-backend.service/momentumx-frontend.service templates + extracted sed logic into /tmp, ran against both a custom ROOT_DIR=/tmp/test_install/Internal-trader and the default ROOT_DIR=/opt/momentumx) - did NOT touch the live running MomentumX app (frontend/backend) which is unrelated to this test, per the request scope. rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: two static systemd .service templates hardcoded /opt/momentumx in WorkingDirectory/PATH/ExecStart; when repo was cloned to /opt/Internal-trader, the deployed unit files still pointed at /opt/momentumx which doesn't exist, causing systemd to fail starting the backend/frontend. Fix: script now computes SCRIPT_DIR/ROOT_DIR from its own real location and, only when ROOT_DIR differs from /opt/momentumx, runs sed -i to replace all /opt/momentumx occurrences in both copied unit files with the real ROOT_DIR before daemon-reload/enable/start. Verified: (1) custom dir case -> WorkingDirectory, PATH env, and ExecStart binary path in momentumx-backend.service and WorkingDirectory in momentumx-frontend.service all correctly rewritten to /tmp/test_install/Internal-trader/... with zero remaining /opt/momentumx references (grep count = 0 on both files); (2) default /opt/momentumx case -> sed block skipped entirely (guard condition false), files remained byte-identical to source templates (diff = empty, grep count unchanged: 3 refs in backend.service, 1 in frontend.service) confirming true no-op regression safety; (3) bash -n syntax check on full script passed with no errors; (4) reviewed start.sh, uninstall_systemd_services.sh, and README.md - no other hardcoded-path bugs found (start.sh already dynamically derives ROOT_DIR; uninstall script has no path deps; README references to /opt/momentumx are advisory documentation only, not functional, minor staleness noted as non-blocking action item).
